title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards and alert tuning
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency breakdown dashboards; tuned alerts to reduce noise and added new SLO-aligned alert thresholds.
body: Motivation: Customers and SREs need finer-grained visibility into per-token cost and latency characteristics to diagnose regressions in cost-per-request and token tail latency. Current dashboards showed only per-request aggregates which masked differences across long-tail requests and multi-turn chats. This PR adds token-level cost and latency metrics, integrates them into new Grafana dashboards and a curated set of panels in Redwood Console, and applies alert tuning to align notifications with the new SLO buckets. Summary of changes: 1) Metrics: Introduced two new Prometheus metrics: redwood_inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket (histogram) and redwood_inference_token_cost_microdollars_total (counter with labels model, tier, route). Added instrumentation points in the serving runtime to record per-token latency (first-token, tail-token, per-step) and to emit cost contributions when token generators finalize. 2) Tracing/logging: Added optional span attributes for token_index and token_latency_ms to the inference span emitted to Jaeger/OTel. Logging: added structured log field token_metrics for debug-level dumps behind a feature flag. 3) Dashboards: New Grafana dashboard templates for token-level breakdowns including: histogram of token latency percentiles, cost contribution waterfall per token, heatmap of token latency by model+route, and a multi-tenant view for Dedicated customers. Also created Redwood Console panels (JSON dashboard fragments) for embedding into per-customer views. 4) Alert tuning: Introduced SLO-aligned alerts: token_latency_p99_exceeds_threshold (rate-based alert with 5m and 1h windows), token_cost_spike_detected (anomaly detector using rolling baseline), and adjusted existing request-level alerts to avoid duplicate paging. 5) Tests and CI: Unit tests for new metric collectors and integration test that validates histogram buckets and cost emission. Dashboard preview CI step added to render JSON panels and validate schema. 6) Docs: Updated observability docs with examples and runbook for interpreting token-level dashboards and handling token_cost_spike alerts. Rollout: feature flag token_level_observability defaults to off for all customers, enabled in staging for 24h, then gradually enabled for 5% of production traffic for Canary, with full rollout after 72h of monitoring. Backwards compatibility: Metrics use stable metric names and add new labels conservatively; existing alert names were kept but thresholds adjusted. Why this change: we observed a 3x increase in cost-per-token variance across recent model quantization rollouts; prior dashboards missed tail latency spikes that caused SLA impacts for several customers. This PR gives SREs and customers the signals needed to triage model/version/regression issues, and reduces noisy alerts by coalescing related conditions. Additional context and links: Linear ENG-1428 covers metric design and ENG-1450 covers dashboard templates. SUP-5021 links to support tickets that motivated alert tuning.
commits: feat: emit token cost counter from runtime (redwood/serving/runtime/token_cost_emitter.go)
feat: tracing: add token_index and token_latency_ms attributes (redwood/serving/tracing/span_attrs.go)
chore: add dashboard preview CI step (ci/dashboard-preview.yaml)
test: unit/integration tests for token metrics (tests/token_metrics_test.go)
ui: add Grafana dashboard json and console fragments (dashboards/token_level_dashboard.json)

ci: address lint failures and fix imports
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Please confirm histogram bucket boundaries are aligned with existing request-level histograms to make comparisons easier. Author reply: Buckets were chosen to match request-level buckets for the 0-500ms range and then use exponential growth beyond 500ms to capture tail; added a comment and unit test to validate alignment.

Priya Singh: Alert noise concern: will token_cost_spike generate duplicate alerts for request-level cost spikes? Author reply: The token_cost_spike alert uses an anomaly detector with baseline subtraction and only fires if request-level_alert is not active; updated rule and added integration test that simulates both conditions.

Liam O'Connor: Can we add labels for model_variant and quantization_profile on the cost metric? Author reply: Added model_variant label but kept quantization_profile out to limit cardinality; added guidance in docs about using logs/trace for per-profile debugging.
rollout_plan: Enable token_level_observability feature flag in staging for 24h, enable for 5% production traffic for Canary and monitor dashboards and alerts for 72h before scaling to 100%. Rollback: toggle feature flag off and revert alert rules via ops playbook. Monitoring: validate token_latency_p95/p99 and token_cost_microdollars rolling baseline during Canary.
notes_for_release: Console: new Token-level Observability dashboard fragment available under Observability > Dashboards > Token-level. Alerts: token_cost_spike and token_latency_p99_exceeds_threshold added to default alerting policy for SRE and Tier1. Customers on Dedicated will see multi-tenant panels; Admins can opt-out via feature flag.
qa_checks: Unit tests cover metric collectors, integration tests validate histogram emission and alert gating, dashboard-preview validates JSON schema, manual QA runbook executed in staging by SRE.
